newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria central bank seeks FPBank liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria central bank seeks FPBank liquidation.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) has asked the Sofia City Court to start liquidation proceedings against First Private Bank (FPB), a BNB official said on Monday.

"On Friday the BNB submitted to the court a request to open a liquidation procedure for First Private on the basis of its earlier decision to retract the bank's licence," a BNB legal department official told Reuters.
A lawyer for FPB said he considered the central bank's request was not well founded because insolvency proceedings under a different law were still pending.

"Bearing in mind that the insolvency procedure is not over and it has been filed under the old banking law, the central bank request for liquidation will create a legal controversy," said the lawyer, who declined to be identified.
The BNB placed FPB in receivership on May 17, 1996, filed an insolvency claim and withdrew its banking licence under the old banking law, which was replaced in June this year.
The central bank said First Private had failed to improve its negative capital to risk assets ratio and to restore regular payments to main creditors during the period of receivership.
The bank owed 100 billion levs to the state and 90 billion levs to the BNB when the BNB sought its insolvency.
In June the Supreme Court ruled in favour of a BNB appeal against a Sofia City court's rejection of the BNB insolvency claim against FPB.
The Supreme Court also returned the case for reconsideration to the Sofia City Court and recommended that it rule FPB insolvent.
Courts have declared nine local commercial banks insolvent so far out of a total of 17 state and private banks against which the BNB has opened bankruptcy proceedings since May 1996.
The BNB has withdrawn insolvency claims against two of the 17 after they were sold. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 981 4145
